links.effect: Classifier-based C2ST achieved perfect detection for quality and co-morbidity subgroup shifts at n=1000; only method detecting sex shifts (0.79 at 30,000 training images); type I error stayed near 5%.
links.quote: Classifier-based tests performed best overall, with perfect detection rates for quality and co-morbidity subgroup shifts at a sample size of 1000.

links.outcome: DR detection performance disparities across patient subgroups (ethnicity, quality, comorbidity, sex)
links.effect: Referable DR sensitivity ranged 0.50 to 0.79 across ethnicities; performance reduced for lower image quality; accuracy dropped for patients with co-morbidities.
links.quote: For example, the referable DR detection performance for different ethnicities ranged between 0.50 and 0.79 sensitivity, and classification performance in all metrics was reduced for images with lower quality.

links.outcome: Subgroup performance gaps hidden by aggregate metrics in DR grading
links.effect: Overall referable DR sensitivity 0.66 but 0.50 for Native American and 0.79 for Indian subgroups; co-morbidity sensitivity 0.82 vs 0.58 without.
links.quote: We found considerable performance differences across subgroups in all reported metrics (right column in Table 1 ).

links.outcome: Statistical threshold-based alerts for detecting distribution shift with controlled false positive rate
links.effect: Type I error remained approximately within the chosen 5% significance level for all tests; detection rates high for many shifts, enabling alerts.
links.quote: For all tests, the type I error (i.e. the false positive detection rate) remained approximately within the chosen significance level (Fig. 3 ).
